source_meta._title: Chorus flowers can be destroyed by projectiles in adventure mode

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.16.5 in a single-player world. Use Creative mode with commands available for setup, then change to Adventure mode before firing the arrow. Default keyboard and mouse controls are assumed unless they have been rebound.
preconditions: Launch an installation/profile using exactly Minecraft Java Edition 1.16.5, the first version listed as affected.
Create or open a world in which commands are available. A newly created Creative-mode single-player world is the simplest setup; no particular seed or coordinates are specified.
Ensure there is a clear, level area where a chorus flower can be placed and approached without other blocks or entities obstructing a bow shot.
Do not use the fixed version 23w42a for this reproduction.

steps.action: Create a new single-player world in Creative mode, or open an existing command-enabled world and enter Creative mode for setup. Wait for terrain generation and chunk loading to finish before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The player can move normally in a loaded area and has access to the Creative inventory.

steps.action: Press E to open the inventory. Open the Creative inventory's Search Items tab, identified by the compass icon.
steps.success_cue: The Creative item catalogue and its search field are visible.

steps.action: Use the search field to obtain one End Stone block, one Chorus Flower, one Bow, and at least one Arrow. For each item, clear the previous search, enter the exact item name, and move the matching item icon into the hotbar or player inventory. Keep the bow in the hotbar and the arrow anywhere in the inventory.
steps.exact_input: End Stone; Chorus Flower; Bow; Arrow
steps.success_cue: The player possesses End Stone, a Chorus Flower, a Bow, and at least one Arrow, with the bow accessible from the hotbar.

steps.action: Close the inventory by pressing E or Esc. Select the hotbar slot containing End Stone using the corresponding number key or mouse wheel.
steps.success_cue: The world view is visible and End Stone is shown as the held item.

steps.action: Aim at the top face of a ground block in the clear test area and use the Place Block control, default right-click, once to place the End Stone as an exposed support block.
steps.success_cue: One End Stone block is present with its top face unobstructed.

steps.action: Select the Chorus Flower in the hotbar. Aim at the exposed top face of the End Stone and use the Place Block control, default right-click, once.
steps.success_cue: A chorus flower is visibly attached to the top of the End Stone.

steps.action: Move approximately 4 to 6 blocks horizontally away from the chorus flower while remaining on roughly the same ground level. Face the flower and ensure no block or entity lies between the player and the flower.
steps.success_cue: The entire chorus flower is visible from a short distance with a clear line of fire.

steps.action: Press T to open the in-game chat input.
steps.success_cue: The chat command input is open and ready to accept text.

steps.action: Enter the Adventure-mode command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter to execute it.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback confirms that the player's game mode is now Adventure mode.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the bow. Confirm that at least one arrow remains in the player inventory.
steps.exact_input: Corresponding hotbar number key or mouse wheel
steps.success_cue: The bow is visible in the player's hand and an arrow is available as ammunition.

steps.action: Place the crosshair over the central visible portion of the chorus flower rather than over the supporting End Stone. Adjust the player's position or aim if necessary, but do not fire yet.
steps.success_cue: The crosshair rests on the chorus flower with an unobstructed trajectory from the bow to the flower.

steps.action: Hold the Use Item control, default right mouse button, until the bow is fully drawn.
steps.success_cue: The bow is in its fully drawn visual state while the crosshair remains aimed at the chorus flower.

steps.action: Release the Use Item control to fire exactly one arrow directly at the chorus flower. Wait only until the arrow reaches the target, then perform no additional attacks or shots.
steps.success_cue: The single fired arrow has reached the chorus flower; the setup and trigger are complete and no second projectile has been fired.

stor.handoff_condition: The player is in Adventure mode and a single arrow fired from the bow has just impacted the placed chorus flower. Stop player input and hand control to the observation subsystem immediately.
uncertainties: The report does not specify single-player versus dedicated-server operation, a world seed, coordinates, or a shooting distance. A command-enabled single-player world and a short unobstructed shot are used as practical implementation choices.
The report only instructs the player to place a chorus flower. End Stone is added as a practical support block so the flower can be placed deterministically in an ordinary test area.
Creative mode is used only to acquire and place the required items efficiently; the projectile is fired only after changing to the report-required Adventure mode.
The report does not state whether controls are rebound. The plan gives the default Java Edition controls.

source_meta._title: Pointed dripstone can be destroyed by tridents in adventure mode

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 21w19a in a single-player world using the integrated server. Create the test arrangement in Creative mode with commands available, then change the player to Adventure mode before throwing the trident. Default keyboard and mouse bindings are described; use the bound equivalents if controls have been changed.
preconditions: Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 21w19a, the first version listed as affected by the report, is installed and launchable.
The executor can create a single-player Creative-mode world in which commands are available.
A mouse or equivalent input capable of holding and releasing the Use Item action is available.
The test area must be inside the world border and outside any condition that prevents normal projectile interaction; an ordinary open area near the single-player spawn is sufficient.
Allow the surrounding terrain to finish loading before constructing or testing the target.

steps.action: Start Minecraft Java Edition using the 21w19a installation and wait for the main menu to become responsive.
steps.success_cue: The main menu displays the snapshot version 21w19a and its buttons respond normally.

steps.action: Create a new single-player world in Creative mode. From the main menu, open Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, and create the world. Leave commands available so the later game-mode command can be executed.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player enters a new world in Creative mode and can fly or instantly break blocks.

steps.action: Wait for the initial world loading to finish. Do not continue while nearby terrain is still appearing or player input is delayed.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is rendered, player movement responds normally, and there is an open patch of ground available.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory, select the Search Items tab, search for "stone", and move one plain Stone block—not Stone Bricks or another variant—into hotbar slot 1. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the screen.
steps.exact_input: E -> Search Items -> type "stone" -> select Stone -> place in hotbar slot 1
steps.success_cue: Hotbar slot 1 contains a plain Stone block.

steps.action: While using the Creative inventory's Search Items tab, clear the previous search, search for "pointed dripstone", and move Pointed Dripstone into hotbar slot 2.
steps.exact_input: Search Items -> type "pointed dripstone" -> select Pointed Dripstone -> place in hotbar slot 2
steps.success_cue: Hotbar slot 2 contains Pointed Dripstone.

steps.action: Clear the search, search for "trident", and move an ordinary unenchanted Trident into hotbar slot 3. No Riptide, Loyalty, or other enchantment is needed.
steps.exact_input: Search Items -> type "trident" -> select Trident -> place in hotbar slot 3
steps.success_cue: Hotbar slot 3 contains an unenchanted Trident.

steps.action: Close the Creative inventory and return to first-person world control.
steps.success_cue: The world view and crosshair are visible, with Stone, Pointed Dripstone, and Trident present in hotbar slots 1, 2, and 3 respectively.

steps.action: Select hotbar slot 1 and place the Stone block on top of an open, level part of the ground. This raised support makes the pointed dripstone easier to strike directly.
steps.exact_input: 1, then right-click the top face of the ground
steps.success_cue: One Stone block stands above the surrounding ground with unobstructed air above and around it.

steps.action: Select hotbar slot 2 and place the Pointed Dripstone on the top face of the Stone support block. Target the upper face of the Stone block rather than one of its sides.
steps.exact_input: 2, then right-click the top face of the Stone block
steps.success_cue: An upward-pointing piece of pointed dripstone is attached to the top of the Stone block and is clearly visible.

steps.action: Move approximately four to six blocks horizontally away from the pointed dripstone. Face the target and ensure there are no blocks, entities, or tall plants between the player and the pointed dripstone.
steps.exact_input: Use movement controls, normally W/A/S/D, then move the mouse to face the target
steps.success_cue: The pointed dripstone is visible from several blocks away with a clear projectile path to it.

steps.action: Change the player from Creative mode to Adventure mode using in-game chat. Press T, enter the command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports that the player's game mode was set to Adventure Mode, and the Adventure-mode indicator briefly appears on screen.

steps.action: Select the Trident in hotbar slot 3 so that it becomes the active held item.
steps.success_cue: The trident is visible in the player's hand and hotbar slot 3 is highlighted.

steps.action: Aim the crosshair directly at the body or upper portion of the pointed dripstone, not at the Stone support block beneath it.
steps.exact_input: Move the mouse until the crosshair is centered on the pointed dripstone
steps.success_cue: The crosshair rests on the pointed dripstone and the projectile path remains unobstructed.

steps.action: Press and hold the Use Item control long enough to fully prepare the trident throw. With default controls, hold the right mouse button for approximately one second; do not release immediately after pressing.
steps.success_cue: The trident is held in its charged throwing pose while the crosshair remains directed at the pointed dripstone.

steps.action: While continuing to aim at the pointed dripstone, release the Use Item control to throw the charged trident directly at it. Do not perform another action before observation begins.
steps.success_cue: The trident has been released toward the pointed dripstone while the player remains in Adventure mode.

stor.handoff_condition: The Adventure-mode player has just released a fully charged trident directly toward the unobstructed pointed dripstone target. Begin observation immediately and monitor the trident's impact without performing additional setup actions.
uncertainties: The report does not provide a world seed, coordinates, or required terrain, so a fresh world and an ordinary open area are used as practical setup choices.
The report does not specify how the pointed dripstone and trident are obtained before entering Adventure mode. Creative inventory setup is used to avoid unrelated crafting, exploration, or combat.

The report does not specify the target's orientation, support block, or throwing distance. An upward-pointing piece on a raised Stone block and a distance of approximately four to six blocks are selected to provide a clear, deterministic projectile target.

The report says to "shoot" the trident but does not state a charge duration. Holding the Use Item control for approximately one second is used to ensure the trident is thrown rather than the input being released too early.
Default controls are assumed. If bindings are customized, use the controls bound to Open Inventory, Open Chat, Select Hotbar Slot, and Use Item.

source_meta._title: Arrows and tridents on fire and stuck in the ground cannot be extinguished by rain

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 24w36a in a fresh singleplayer Creative-mode world with commands enabled. Use an open, unsheltered location in a biome where precipitation falls as rain. Default controls are assumed: T for chat, E for inventory, number keys or mouse wheel for hotbar selection, and right mouse button for using the bow.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher can launch the exact affected snapshot 24w36a; do not use the fix version 25w02a.
Use a fresh singleplayer test world so there are no previously fired arrows that could be selected by the nearest-arrow selector @n[type=minecraft:arrow].
Commands must be permitted. Creating the test world in Creative mode is the simplest way to provide command access, although the report does not require a particular game mode.

The test location must have a clear view of the sky and exposed solid ground, such as the top surface of grass, dirt, or stone. Do not perform the test beneath trees, roofs, caves, or other blocks that can intercept rain.
Use a biome where /weather rain produces visible rain rather than no precipitation or snow; an open plains or forest location is suitable.
Use the commands exactly as written, including capitalization, selectors, component syntax, and the leading slash.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select or create an installation for snapshot 24w36a, launch it, and wait for the main menu to finish loading.
steps.success_cue: The main menu identifies the running Minecraft Java Edition version as 24w36a.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, create a new world in Creative mode, and enter the world. Wait until surrounding terrain is rendered and player movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is in a loaded 24w36a world and has permission to execute commands.

steps.action: Move to flat, exposed ground in a rain-capable biome. Stand where the sky directly above both the player and the intended arrow landing point is unobstructed. Ensure no other arrows are present nearby.
steps.success_cue: There is an exposed solid ground surface several blocks in front of the player, with no roof or foliage overhead and no other arrow entities nearby.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Enter the weather-clear command exactly as supplied, including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The game acknowledges the weather command and begins or maintains clear weather.

steps.action: Wait until any previous precipitation has stopped and the exposed test area is visibly clear. Do not continue while rain or snow particles are still falling at the test location.
steps.success_cue: No precipitation particles are falling at the player or the intended arrow landing point.

steps.action: Press T, enter the supplied command that gives the player a Flame-enchanted bow, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command succeeds and a bow with Flame level 1 is present in the player's inventory.

steps.action: Press T, enter the supplied command that gives the player an arrow, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command succeeds and at least one arrow is present in the player's inventory.

steps.action: Press E to open the inventory. If necessary, move the Flame-enchanted bow into one of the nine hotbar slots at the bottom of the inventory. Leave at least one arrow anywhere in the player inventory. Close the inventory with E, then select the bow's hotbar slot using its number key or the mouse wheel.
steps.success_cue: The Flame-enchanted bow is visible in the player's hand, and an arrow remains available in the inventory.

steps.action: Look downward and aim the crosshair at the exposed top face of a solid ground block approximately 3 to 5 blocks away. Choose a point that remains directly exposed to the sky and is close enough that the resulting arrow will be the nearest arrow to the player.
steps.success_cue: The crosshair is on an exposed horizontal ground surface with no entity or block overhang between the bow and the target point.

steps.action: Press and hold the use-item control, which is the right mouse button by default, until the bow reaches full draw.
steps.success_cue: The bow is fully drawn while the crosshair remains aimed at the exposed ground.

steps.action: Release the right mouse button once to shoot the Flame arrow into the targeted ground surface.
steps.success_cue: One arrow has been fired toward the selected ground block.

steps.action: Wait only until the fired arrow is visibly embedded in the ground and has stopped moving. Confirm that it is aflame before changing the weather. Keep the player near this arrow and perform the remaining steps promptly so the projectile does not despawn.
steps.success_cue: A single visibly flaming arrow is stationary and embedded in exposed ground near the player.

steps.action: Press T, enter the supplied entity-data command, and press Enter. Record the numeric Fire value returned for the nearest arrow, but do not remove or disturb the arrow.
steps.success_cue: Chat returns a numeric Fire tag value for an arrow rather than reporting that no matching entity was found.

steps.action: Leave the arrow embedded and wait approximately 2 seconds without shooting another projectile, moving far away, changing dimension, or altering the weather. This short delay makes the two pre-rain queries meaningfully separated in time.
steps.success_cue: The same arrow remains stationary in the exposed ground and is still the only nearby arrow.

steps.action: Press T, enter the same supplied entity-data command again, and press Enter. Record the second numeric Fire value without interpreting the result.
steps.success_cue: Chat returns a second numeric Fire tag value for the same nearest embedded arrow.

steps.action: Press T, enter the supplied rain command, and press Enter. Do not move or disturb the embedded arrow.
steps.success_cue: The game acknowledges the weather command and begins transitioning the world to rain.

steps.action: Wait at the test location until rain particles are visibly falling through the open sky at the embedded arrow's exact position. Keep the arrow loaded and within a few blocks of the player.
steps.success_cue: The same embedded arrow is present, and visible rain is falling directly at its unsheltered location.

steps.action: While the arrow remains embedded and exposed to active rain, press T, enter the supplied entity-data command for the third time, and press Enter. Record the returned Fire value without evaluating either the visual or data result.
steps.success_cue: Chat has returned a third numeric Fire tag value for the same embedded arrow while rain is visibly falling at the arrow's position.

stor.handoff_condition: The originally flaming arrow is still embedded in exposed ground, visible rain is falling directly at its position, and the third Fire-tag query has just returned in chat. Hand control to the observation subsystem to inspect the projectile's visual and entity-data state.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode. This plan uses Creative mode as a practical way to guarantee command access and simplify item handling; the reported trigger itself does not state that Creative mode is required.
The report provides no world seed, biome, or coordinates. The executor must choose an exposed location in a biome where precipitation appears as rain rather than snow or no precipitation.

The report says to execute the first data command twice but does not specify the delay between executions. A delay of approximately 2 seconds is added so measurable game time passes while keeping the procedure well within the arrow's lifetime.

Although the issue title includes both arrows and tridents, the supplied reproduction procedure provides exact commands and actions only for the arrow variant. This plan therefore reproduces only the explicitly documented arrow path.

The report does not explicitly require singleplayer, but the supplied attachment filenames identify singleplayer recordings. A fresh singleplayer world is selected to avoid unrelated nearby arrows and selector ambiguity.

source_meta._title: Projectiles don't collide with the world border

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 14w17a in a singleplayer Creative-mode Superflat world with commands/cheats enabled. Use the normal first-person view. The instructions name the default controls: T for chat, E for inventory, number keys 1–9 for hotbar selection, and right-click for Use Item; use the equivalent bound controls if they have been changed.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact Java Edition snapshot listed as the recommended version: Minecraft 14w17a. Do not use fix version 24w33a.
Use a new disposable world so changing the world-border center and size does not affect an existing save.
Use Creative mode and enable commands/cheats so the supplied /worldborder commands can be executed and a Snowball can be obtained without random exploration.
Use a Superflat world as a deterministic execution choice; the report does not specify a seed, coordinates, or terrain, and a flat world provides a clear projectile path.
Keep at least one empty hotbar slot available for the Snowball.

steps.action: Start Minecraft Java Edition using the Minecraft 14w17a installation/profile and wait for the main menu to load.
steps.success_cue: The lower-left version label on the main menu identifies the running version as Minecraft 14w17a.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, then select Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Click the Game Mode button until it displays Game Mode: Creative.
steps.success_cue: Creative is displayed as the selected game mode.

steps.action: Select More World Options... to open the additional world-generation settings.
steps.success_cue: The screen containing World Type and Allow Cheats is visible.

steps.action: Click World Type until it displays World Type: Superflat.
steps.success_cue: Superflat is displayed as the selected world type.

steps.action: Set Allow Cheats to ON. If it is already ON because Creative mode was selected, leave it unchanged.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen displays Allow Cheats: ON.

steps.action: Return from More World Options if necessary, select Create New World, and wait for world generation to finish. Do not move away from the initial location after control is granted.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing on the Superflat surface, nearby terrain is rendered, and movement and camera controls respond normally.

steps.action: Press the Chat control, default T, to open in-game chat.
steps.success_cue: A chat input line is visible and ready to accept a command.

steps.action: Enter the report's world-border center command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter. Both tildes refer to the player's current horizontal position: the first is X and the second is Z.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted without a syntax or permission error, and chat reports that the world-border center was changed.

steps.action: Without moving from the newly established center, press the Chat control, default T, again.
steps.success_cue: The chat input line is open again.

steps.action: Enter the report's world-border size command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter. The value 20 sets the square border to twenty blocks wide.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted without an error, chat reports that the world-border width was set to 20 blocks, and the nearby world-border walls become visible around the player.

steps.action: Wait until the border has finished resizing, surrounding terrain remains rendered, and movement and camera controls respond normally. Because the player remained at the center of a 20-block-wide border, each nearest side should be approximately 10 blocks away.
steps.success_cue: A stable square world border surrounds the player, with the player still safely inside it near the center.

steps.action: Press the Inventory control, default E, to open the Creative inventory.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory interface is open and the hotbar slots are visible along its bottom edge.

steps.action: Open the Search Items tab, identified by the compass icon, select its search field, and search for Snowball. With an English interface, enter the text shown in exact_input.
steps.success_cue: A Snowball item appears among the filtered Creative inventory results.

steps.action: Move a stack of Snowballs from the search result into an empty hotbar slot. One reliable method is to left-click the Snowball result to pick up a stack, then left-click an empty slot in the hotbar row at the bottom of the inventory.
steps.success_cue: A Snowball stack is visible in a numbered hotbar slot.

steps.action: Close the Creative inventory by pressing E or Escape.
steps.success_cue: First-person world view is restored and the hotbar containing the Snowball stack is visible.

steps.action: Select the Snowball's hotbar slot by pressing its corresponding number key, 1 through 9, or by scrolling to it.
steps.success_cue: The Snowball slot has the active-slot highlight and a Snowball is visible in the player's hand.

steps.action: Rotate the camera while remaining inside the border until one of the four nearby world-border walls is directly ahead. Do not move through the wall or outside the border.
steps.success_cue: A world-border wall is centered in the player's forward view approximately 10 blocks away.

steps.action: Adjust the crosshair so it points toward the world-border wall through unobstructed air at approximately eye level. Do not aim downward at the Superflat ground and do not place any block between the player and the border.
steps.success_cue: The straight path from the player's hand to the targeted part of the world border is clear of blocks and entities.

steps.action: Use the selected Snowball once by pressing the Use Item control, default right-click, while maintaining the aim established in the previous step.
steps.success_cue: One Snowball has been launched directly toward the world-border wall on an unobstructed path.

stor.handoff_condition: The Snowball has just been launched directly toward the nearby world-border wall from inside the border. Hand control immediately to the observation subsystem before changing aim, moving the player, throwing another projectile, or otherwise altering the scene.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a world seed, coordinates, terrain type, game mode, or singleplayer versus multiplayer. A new singleplayer Creative Superflat world is selected only as the simplest deterministic environment that supports the supplied commands and provides a clear projectile path.

The Creative inventory's displayed item names depend on the selected language. The exact search input "snowball" assumes an English interface; in another language, use the localized name or visually locate the Snowball item.

External verification confirms that /worldborder was introduced in Java Edition 14w17a and supports the supplied center and set command forms; therefore the report's commands are preserved without modernization. ([pt.minecraft.wiki](https://pt.minecraft.wiki/w/Barreira_do_mundo?utm_source=openai))

The report states that all types of projectiles are affected but proposes a Snowball as its example. This plan tests one Snowball once, which is the minimum safe trigger supported by the report; it does not add repeated throws or alternate projectiles.

source_meta._title: Tridents or arrows shot through lava sometimes don't catch fire

stor.environment: Unmodified Minecraft Java Edition 1.4.7 in a single-player Creative-mode world, using mouse and keyboard controls. Use arrows and a bow for this version-specific reproduction path. No seed, coordinates, server, datapack, or special graphics setting is required by the report.
preconditions: A playable Minecraft Java Edition 1.4.7 installation is available.
Use an unmodified client so that mods do not change projectile or fluid behavior.
Create or use a Creative-mode world so the setup materials can be obtained deterministically.
Have an open, approximately level area with at least 25 blocks of unobstructed horizontal space.
Use the configured controls corresponding to Inventory (default E), Use Item (default right mouse button), Attack/Break (default left mouse button), and movement.
The following items must be available from the Creative inventory: stone or another nonflammable full block, one block of diamond, one lava bucket, one bow, and at least one stack of arrows.

steps.action: Start Minecraft Java Edition using the affected release selected for this reproduction. Do not use the listed fix version 25w02a.
steps.success_cue: The title screen identifies the running version as Minecraft 1.4.7.

steps.action: From the title screen, create a single-player Creative-mode world: select Singleplayer, select Create New World, cycle the Game Mode option until it reads Creative, and create the world. No particular seed is required.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player spawns in a world and can fly and place or break blocks immediately.

steps.action: Wait before building until the nearby terrain is rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The ground and surrounding chunks are visible, and the player can move without waiting for terrain to appear.

steps.action: Press the Inventory control, default E, to open the Creative inventory. Locate stone or another nonflammable full block, a block of diamond, a lava bucket, a bow, and arrows. Place the building block, diamond block, lava bucket, and bow into hotbar slots, and place at least one stack of arrows in the inventory or hotbar. Close the inventory with E or Esc.
steps.exact_input: E; place stone, Block of Diamond, Lava Bucket, Bow, and at least 64 Arrows into the player inventory; E or Esc
steps.success_cue: The hotbar contains the building blocks, diamond block, lava bucket, and bow, and the inventory contains arrows.

steps.action: Move to an open, approximately level location with enough room for a lava column, a shooting marker about 10 blocks away, and a target wall on the opposite side.
steps.exact_input: W/A/S/D; double-tap Space to begin Creative flight if needed
steps.success_cue: At least 25 blocks of clear horizontal space are available along one straight line.

steps.action: Using the nonflammable building block, construct a 5-by-5-block horizontal basin floor at ground level. Place a one-block-high border on top of the outer edge of that floor, leaving a 3-by-3 interior. This basin is only intended to contain lava that reaches the bottom of the test column.
steps.exact_input: Select the stone hotbar slot; right-click to place blocks
steps.success_cue: A 5-by-5 nonflammable floor with a one-block-high perimeter surrounds a 3-by-3 recessed interior.

steps.action: Identify the exact center block of the 5-by-5 basin floor. Build a temporary vertical pillar five blocks high starting on top of that center block.
steps.exact_input: Right-click five times while aiming at the top face of the center block and then each newly placed block
steps.success_cue: A five-block-tall temporary pillar rises from the center of the basin.

steps.action: At the height of the pillar's top block, place one nonflammable block directly adjacent to each of its four horizontal faces. These four blocks must surround the top block to the north, south, east, and west while leaving the diagonal corners open.
steps.exact_input: Right-click to place four blocks, one against each horizontal side of the top pillar block
steps.success_cue: The pillar's top block is surrounded horizontally by four nonflammable blocks.

steps.action: Break all five blocks of the temporary center pillar using the Attack/Break control, default left-click. Do not break the four blocks surrounding its former top position.
steps.exact_input: Left-click each of the five temporary pillar blocks
steps.success_cue: The center is an open vertical air column, with four floating blocks surrounding the top position on its horizontal sides.

steps.action: Choose one horizontal direction through the basin center as the shooting direction. On one side of the basin, count approximately 10 horizontal block positions from the basin center. Replace the ground block at that position with the diamond block. This is the required standing marker from the report.
steps.exact_input: Select Block of Diamond; left-click the ground block at the marker position; right-click to place the diamond block
steps.success_cue: A single diamond block marks a firing position approximately 10 blocks from the center of the future lava column.

steps.action: On the side of the basin directly opposite the diamond block, construct a target wall from nonflammable blocks. Place it approximately five blocks beyond the basin center and make it at least three blocks wide and four blocks high. Center the wall on the straight line from the diamond block through the basin center.
steps.exact_input: Select the nonflammable building block; right-click to construct a 3-block-wide by 4-block-high wall
steps.success_cue: The diamond block, basin center, and middle column of the target wall lie on one straight horizontal line.

steps.action: Fly to the four-block holder above the basin. Select the lava bucket and place one lava source in the central air position surrounded horizontally by the four holder blocks. Aim at an inward-facing side of a holder block so the lava is placed in the center rather than on top of the holder.
steps.exact_input: Select Lava Bucket; right-click an inward-facing holder-block face
steps.success_cue: A single lava source occupies the center of the four holder blocks and a vertical lava stream begins descending into the basin.

steps.action: Wait until the lava has descended to the basin and finished visibly updating. Confirm that the elevated portion forms a continuous vertical lava column between the diamond marker and target wall. Do not shoot through the spreading lava at basin-floor level; the intended line passes horizontally through the vertical column above the border.
steps.success_cue: The lava column is continuous, the bottom flow is contained by the basin, and fluid movement has stabilized.

steps.action: Move onto the diamond block and stop approximately in its center. Face directly toward the lava column and target wall.
steps.exact_input: W/A/S/D; move the crosshair to face the lava and wall
steps.success_cue: The player is standing on the diamond block with the lava column centered between the player and target wall.

steps.action: Select the bow's hotbar slot. Verify that arrows remain in the inventory.
steps.exact_input: Press the number key corresponding to the Bow hotbar slot
steps.success_cue: The bow is visible in the player's hand, and at least one arrow stack is available.

steps.action: Without leaving the diamond block, align the crosshair with the center column of the target wall at approximately the player's eye height. Ensure that the straight sight line crosses the central portion of the vertical lava column rather than passing beside or above it.
steps.exact_input: Move the mouse until the crosshair is centered on the target wall through the lava column
steps.success_cue: The crosshair, center of the lava column, and center of the target wall are aligned.

steps.action: Hold the Use Item control, default right mouse button, until the bow reaches its fully drawn visual state. Keep the crosshair aligned and do not move off the diamond block.
steps.exact_input: Hold right-click until the bow is fully drawn
steps.success_cue: The bow is visibly at full draw while the crosshair remains aimed through the lava at the target wall.

steps.action: Release the Use Item control to fire the first fully drawn arrow through the lava column toward the target wall. This is the first trigger action for the behavior under inspection.
steps.success_cue: The first arrow has been launched on a path through the lava column toward the target wall.

steps.action: Remain on the diamond block and repeat the same controlled full-draw shot nine additional times: realign through the center of the lava if necessary, hold the Use Item control until the bow is fully drawn, and release it. Do not intentionally vary the firing position or aim between shots. The report specifies multiple projectiles because the condition is intermittent; ten total shots provide a bounded test series.
steps.exact_input: For each of 9 additional shots: hold right-click until full draw, then release right-click
steps.success_cue: A total of 10 fully drawn arrows have been launched from the diamond block along the same line through the lava column.

stor.handoff_condition: The controlled firing series has begun at step 18 and, after step 19, a total of 10 full-draw arrows have just been fired from the diamond block through the same stabilized lava column toward the target wall. The observation subsystem should inspect each projectile during this firing series without changing the player's position, aim line, lava setup, or game version.
uncertainties: The attachment showing the original setup was named in the report but its image contents were not supplied. The plan therefore uses the report comment's textual alternative: one lava source, a firing position about 10 blocks away, and a fully drawn bow shot through the lava.

The exact attachment geometry is unknown. The elevated source holder, containment basin, and target wall are practical construction choices intended to create a stable, clearly aligned lava crossing without changing the stated trigger action.
The report does not specify a game mode. Creative mode is selected only to make setup and item acquisition deterministic.
The report says to fire multiple projectiles but does not provide an exact count. This plan uses 10 total arrows as a bounded test series for the intermittent condition.

The arrow branch is used because the report permits either tridents or arrows and the selected first affected version is Minecraft 1.4.7. No trident-specific procedure is required for this reproduction path.
Comment 16 mentions confirmation in 24w45a, but that version is not present in the report's Affects versions field and has therefore not been added to affected_versions.
